Layering for Winter Hikes

Three layers keep you warm and dry on a cold day out.

Base layer

Merino or synthetic, close to the skin. Its job is to move sweat away so you don't get cold when you stop. Avoid cotton: it holds water and dries slowly.

Mid layer

A fleece or a light synthetic jacket traps warm air. Take it off before a long climb and put it back on at the top.

Shell

A waterproof, breathable jacket against wind and rain. Pit zips help on the way up.
